thesis: S&P Global sells financial intelligence: credit ratings on debt issuance, index licensing tied to benchmark AUM, Market Intelligence data subscriptions, Platts commodity benchmarks, and Mobility analytics (spin planned mid-2026). **[Fact]** Customers pay transaction fees when markets issue debt, recurring subscriptions for data, and AUM-linked index fees. **[Fact]** FY2025 revenue was **$15,336M** with operating income **$6,478M** and net income **$4,471M** (`investor-documents/sec-edgar/10-K_20260211_rpt20251231_acc0000064040_26_000013.htm`). **[Fact]** Q1 2026 revenue was **$4,171M** (+10% vs **$3,777M**) with GAAP diluted EPS **$4.69** vs **$3.54** and operating income **$2,002M** vs **$1,578M** (`investor-documents/sec-edgar/10-Q_20260428_rpt20260331_acc0000064040_26_000024.htm`). The business earns toll-like fees with minimal principal risk on core operations.
why_market_wrong: No clear mispricing signal or dated payoff. **[Inference]** Quality compounders rarely trade to a 15% IRR; the market prices covenant-required ratings and S&P 500 index entrenchment at a premium. **[Inference]** May 2026 Market Intelligence leadership transition may create temporary concern, but 2026 guidance was reiterated per prior 8-K. Return is franchise earnings at price unless an issuance drought forces a cyclical re-rating.
